target_customer: Hospitals and oncology clinics in India and Singapore that pay for software to monitor cancer patients after discharge
problem: Hospitals cannot support chronic and cancer patients once they go home, so toxicities go unmanaged and emergency readmissions rise. India has very few oncologists per patient.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to hospitals (remote patient monitoring platform called CareShare)

founders.name: Monika Mehta
prior_employers: Chugai Pharma, Roche group, Singapore (Senior Scientist)
founders.background_notes: Scientist and clinical researcher. Said in a later interview that the first idea, predicting response to immunotherapy, was pivoted 3 to 4 times (reported via search result, not opened).

founders.name: Dheeraj Mundhra
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built AI products in finance and healthcare over about seven years; employers not listed.

competitors.name: Practo, mFine and other Indian telehealth startups
competitors.what: General telehealth and consultation apps named as potential competitors in a founder interview, not oncology specific

technical_complexity.rationale: A symptom tracking and alerting app plus clinician dashboard is standard software. The hard parts were clinical workflow integration and hospital onboarding, not the technology.

defensibility.rationale: Hospital integrations create some lock in, but the company stayed at two people and hospital in-house monitoring teams were an easy alternative.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent is documented as copying or buying it. One directory says the product company did not continue after 2024 and now runs as an advisory practice, a single unverified source.

market_need_then: India had about 2,200 oncologists for 1.38 billion people according to the YC description, and COVID-19 in 2020 pushed hospitals toward remote monitoring. The product was first used for COVID-19 home isolation patients before moving to cancer.

branding.domain_note: Operates at zealth-ai.com, not an exact zealth.com match.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found; only directory listings and a 2020 interview. The name resembles Zealth-like health names and was never a growth driver.

pivots.to: Remote monitoring of COVID-19 patients, then cancer patients (CareShare)
pivots.why: Founder statement of 3 to 4 pivots from the first idea; the reason is not given in sources opened

outcome_analysis: Zealth entered YC in Winter 2021 with two founders and a plausible need in Indian oncology, and claimed adoption by 21 hospitals. No institutional funding round was found, and one directory says the product company stopped in 2024 and became an advisory practice, which conflicts with the YC Active label. The cause is not public, so the failure factor is a tentative reading from the absence of any funding and a team that stayed at one or two people.
notes: Funding figures are unverified aggregator claims: about 125K USD (one strategic round) and about 225K to 230K USD total on record; an Antler link appears in one directory only and a CB Insights listing ties Antler to the CEO's work history, not as an investor. Not recorded as rounds. The 2024 advisory status and the 21 hospitals and 20,000 patients figures are company or single directory claims. A search for shutdown or layoff news found nothing about this company. YC marks it Active.
